arml-local-2011-relay-1-1.prompt: Farmer Martin has some chickens and some cows. He looks in his barn and counts $58$ legs. He sees $17$ heads on the animals in his barn. Assuming that all chickens have two legs and all cows have four legs (and all animals have one head), compute the number of chickens in the barn.

arml-local-2011-relay-2-1.prompt: Let $S$ be a set of nine distinct integers. Six of the elements of the set are $1,2,3,5,8$, and $13$. Compute the number of possible values for the median of $S$.

arml-local-2011-relay-2-2.prompt: Let $T=7$. Compute the largest integer $K$ such that a $1\times K$ rectangle can be completely covered by an arrangement of $T$ disks of radius $1$.

arml-local-2011-relay-2-3.prompt: Let $T=12$. $ABC$ and $BAD$ are congruent $30$-$60$-$90$ triangles, both with $AB$ as their hypotenuse of length $T$. If $C$ and $D$ are distinct points in the plane and the intersection of the triangles has positive area, compute the area of the region common to both $ABC$ and $BAD$.

arml-local-2011-relay-3-1.prompt: Compute the number of positive integers greater than one whose fourth powers are factors of $9!$.

arml-local-2011-relay-3-3.prompt: Let $T=4$. Compute the number of ordered pairs of integers $(x,y)$ such that $0\le x\le T$, $0\le y\le T$, $x+y\ne T$, and $x+y\ne T+2$.

arml-local-2011-relay-3-4.prompt: Let $T=17$. Let $S$ be the set of all positive multiples of $9$ that contain at least one $2$ in their base-$10$ representation. The smallest element of $S$ is $27$. Compute the $T^{\text{th}}$ smallest element of $S$.

arml-local-2011-relay-3-5.prompt: Let $T=342$. Compute the minimum perimeter of a rectangle with integer side lengths and area $T$.

arml-local-2011-relay-3-6.prompt: Let $T=74$. Compute the number of three element subsets $S$ of $\{1,2,\ldots,T\}$ such that the elements of $S$ can be arranged into an arithmetic sequence.
